correctness.rationale: The adjacency invariant decomposition is direct and exact. The loss equals one quarter of a phase-error sum plus a nonnegative spectral coherence defect, and is comparable to squared eigenphase distances. Nearest odd phases produce opposite-parity integers; their nonzero quadratic integer norm gives the explicit lower bound valid for all times. Bounded continued fractions for an irrational quadratic slope yield inverse-linear inhomogeneous half-integer approximation at an index within the deadline, hence quadratic inverse-deadline fidelity loss at an admissible time. Exact finite adjacency checks and independent small-time exponentials support but do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem 14(2a) and Example 3 of arXiv:2201.02720 are acknowledged as already proving proper PGST and no PST for this exact defective clique, so neither is the novelty claim. The assessed contribution is a uniform all-time explicit lower bound and matching upper bound for the optimal fixed-deadline infidelity, which yield a sharp quadratic time-to-error exponent. The inspected close source does not assert these finite-window rates; arXiv:2208.08971 offers general PGST decision and supremum algorithms without this sharp rate. Originality remains subject to the named general quantitative-recurrence literature risk.
residual_risks: A broader quantitative two-frequency quantum recurrence theorem indexed under Diophantine approximation, or other terminology, might specialize to the sharp exponent even though the directly relevant primary transfer papers do not state it.
The explicit upper coefficient uses an unspecified, albeit finite and computable, bound on periodic continued-fraction partial quotients, and is not an optimal constant.

value.rationale: The natural practically decisive question is how much time is needed to attain target fidelity in an all-to-all quantum network with one missing coupling. A known PGST existence result leaves this rate undetermined. The new matching upper and lower bounds establish a sharp order-of-growth resource law for every fixed admissible graph order, including a pointwise obstruction; no n-uniform or optimal-constant claim is made.
